entries.description: Gives the elementalist Form Water at 0. The character also has the Phlegmatic Personality Trait, equal to his Warping Score plus a fifth of the Form (rounded up).

entries.name: Embitterment
entries.summary: Make someone hostile to a target of your choice; grants Embitterment 1.
entries.description: You may make someone hostile to a target of your choice. Choosing this Virtue confers the Ability Embitterment 1. Community Gloss This ability is associated with the Nemthengacha magical tradition, described in Ars Magica Definitive Edition, Chapter Seven: Hermetic Magic, and in Tales of Mythic Europe Chapter Two: The Champion's Portion.

entries.name: Emir
entries.summary: Muslim noble warrior; same as the Knight Virtue, typically also skilled in hunting, religion and culture.
entries.description: This is the same as the Knight Virtue, though due to the rather different upbringing of Muslim emirs, you are likely to be as skilled with hunting, religious teachings, and culture as you are with martial pursuits.

entries.name: Empathy
entries.summary: Grants Empathy at 1: Stamina-based rites via a Fatigue-costing trance; extra Fatigue doubles bonuses and maximum level.
entries.description: See Chapter 6: Faerie Wizardry for a full description of this Faerie Method. Choosing this Virtue gives the character Empathy with an initial score of 1.

entries.name: Enchant Casting Tools
entries.summary: Enchant a spell's casting tool (Lab Total at least twice effect level) with fast, multiple or quiet casting, casting bonus, summon or dismiss.
entries.description: Soon after Fenistour invented casting tools, allowing Verditius magi to cast formulaic spells, her filii sought to develop a method of enchanting them, hoping to further compensate their brethren for their clumsiness at spell casting. Achieving their goal in the ninth century, Verditius magi began sharing these secrets, developing Scripts for their fellows to more easily become Initiated into this Mystery. This is particularly useful for those adventurous Verditius magi who like casting spells outside of their laboratories. This is a very common Inner House Mystery among Verditius magi in the 13th century. The magus may enchant his casting tools to mirror certain effects of mastered spells, as well as allowing casting bonuses when he uses them. This is a laboratory process, requiring a season spent working in a Hermetic laboratory. Each casting tool can only be enchanted once, even if it has more than one property, and the magus must be able to finish the enchantment in a single season as if he were creating a lesser enchanted device. Enchanted casting tools cannot be instilled with other magical powers, and cannot be used as a base for a lesser or greater enchanted item. To enchant a casting tool, compare the magus's Technique and Form Lab Total to the level of the spell that the casting tool is associated with. Since the magus is carving minor Verditius runes into his casting tool, you may add his Philosophiae score to the Lab Total. If the magus has a Craft Ability that could include making the tools, you may also add his Craft score. Because enchanted casting tools become permanent arcane connections to the magus, add his Hubris Personality score to the Lab Total. The magus also receives a bonus for knowing the spell in the first place, adding the magnitude of the spell to the Lab Total, much like the bonus received from knowing a similar spell (ArM5, page 101). The level for the effect is equal to the level of the spell plus the adjustment for any additional powers the magus includes, and the magus's Lab Total must be at least twice the effect level, so that he can perform the enchantment in one season. Enchant Casting Tools Lab Total: Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory + Aura Modifier + Philosophiae + Hubris + Magnitude of Known Spell + Craft (If Applicable) The base effect level of the casting tool equals the level of the spell it is used for. The effect level increases based upon the additional effects the magus wishes to enchant it with. There is no limit to the number of effects he can add, as long as his Lab Total plus bonuses is double the final effect level. Increase Casting Tool Effect: +2 Fast Casting (as a mastered spell). +2 Multiple Casting (as a mastered spell). This allows one additional spell, additional spells may be added for a +2 effect level increase each. +2 Quiet Casting (as a mastered spell). This can be taken twice to cast the spell silently. + x Increase spell casting roll by x. +10 Summon casting tool. The casting tool appears in the magus's hand no matter where he stores it, although this is usually in his sanctum. +10 Dismiss casting tool. The casting tool disappears from the magus's person, traveling to a place chosen at the time of enchantment. An Arcane Connection to this place must be bound into the item, and so is usually the magus's sanctum. Enchanting casting tools requires vis. The magus must spend one pawn of Techniqueor Form-specifi c vis per 10 levels of the final effect level total, rounded up. Initiation of Enchant Casting Tools Ease Factor: 15 (Minor Virtue known to the Mystagogue) Script Bonus: +9 Script Details: The Mystagogue spends a season with the Initiate, creating casting tools one after another (+3). The Initiate must know the exact time and date that she was Initiated into the House's Outer Mystery. On an anniversary of that date, she ritualistically buries all her casting tools in a Magic regio (+3). If the Initiation is successful, the Initiate learns the Inner House Minor Mystery Enchant Casting Tools. The buried casting tools are destroyed and the Initiate receives the Minor Flaw Limited Magic Resistance to Vim (Ordeal +3).

entries.name: Enchanting {ability}
entries.summary: Magically induce emotions and beliefs through one art form (music, dance, storytelling, craft); grants Enchanting (Ability) 1.
entries.description: When you set your mind to it, you can magically induce emotions and beliefs in others with a particular kind of artistic expression: music, dance, drawing, storytelling, even craft-work. Choosing this Virtue confers the Ability Enchanting (Ability) 1 (page 164).

entries.name: Enchanting Storytelling
entries.summary: As Enchanting Music, but worked by telling a story or reciting poetry; a Profession: Storyteller or Poet roll ensures the tale isn't botched.
entries.description: A variant of the Enchanting Music Virtue called Enchanting Storytelling is possessed by some bards; it is identical to the Supernatural Ability (ArM5, page 65) in every way other than the fact that the bard tells a story or recites poetry rather than sings or plays music. A Profession: Storyteller or Poet roll should be made to ensure that the tale is not botched when using this Supernatural Ability.

entries.name: Enchantment
entries.summary: Grants Enchantment at 1: Presence-based rites cast through performances that build bonuses; may use simple dice for rites.
entries.description: See Chapter 6: Faerie Wizardry for a full description of this Faerie Method. Choosing this Virtue gives the character Enchantment with an initial score of 1.

entries.name: Enduring Constitution
entries.summary: -1 to Fatigue-level penalties and to total wound penalty (not below 0); +3 to resist pain.
entries.description: You can withstand pain and fatigue. Decrease the penalties for reduced Fatigue levels by one point, and reduce your total penalty from wounds by one point (but not below zero). You also get +3 on rolls to resist pain.

entries.name: Enduring Magic
entries.summary: Non-Ritual spell durations multiplied by a secret simple die (Concentration, Momentary and Ring unaffected).
entries.description: The effects of your spells tend to last longer than usual (though Concentration, Momentary, and Ring spells remain just that). The storyguide secretly rolls a simple die; multiply the spell's normal duration by the number rolled. This is usually, but not always, a good thing. This Virtue does not affect the duration of Ritual spells.

entries.name: Energy Magic
entries.summary: Knows extra Creo and Perdo Corpus guidelines that restore or drain Fatigue.
entries.description: The magus can use additional Creo Corpus and Perdo Corpus guidelines (an Integration breakthrough from the folk witches). Ritual spells of Momentary Duration truly restore Fatigue levels; with other Durations the restored levels return as Long-Term Fatigue when the spell ends.

entries.name: Fast Caster (Runes)
entries.summary: Carves rune scripts in half the time, and can fast-cast a rune spell without name or description.
entries.description: The vitki inscribes rune scripts accurately in half the normal time. The vitki can also fast-cast a rune spell, much as magi fast-cast spontaneous spells, but must leave off their name and the description of the effect.

entries.name: Hedge Wizard (Social Status)
entries.summary: Member of a hedge tradition: Opens a Gifted member's Gift to its magic; access to Finesse, Magic Lore and Penetration.
entries.description: The free Social Status every hedge tradition grants its members. For a Gifted character it Opens The Gift to the tradition's Arts and Abilities, which become favored; for an unGifted one it brings only the social side, and each power still needs its own Virtue. It gives access to the Arcane Abilities Finesse, Magic Lore and Penetration. Whether it combines with other statuses, Wealthy or Poor depends on the tradition. Several traditions have their own named version (Folk Witch, Gruagach, Mathematicus of Bologna, Vitki).

entries.name: Greater Magical Defenses
entries.summary: Doubles every Magical Defense bonus from the tradition's Arts and Abilities.
entries.description: Every Magical Defense bonus the character's hedge Arts or Supernatural Abilities give him is doubled. It does not affect true Magic Resistance such as the Parma Magica.

entries.name: Known Hedge Wizard
entries.summary: Known as a hedge wizard, drawing the attention of the Order and others.
entries.description: The character is known to be a practitioner of hedge magic, which brings the attention of magi, the Church and the local people, and stories with it.

entries.name: Nightwalker Tradition ({tradition})
entries.summary: Member of a regional nightwalker tradition (benandanti, Hounds of God, kresniki, kudlaki, taltós).
entries.description: Membership of a regional nightwalker tradition, such as the benandanti, the Hounds of God, the kresniki, the kudlaki or the taltós, is a Free Virtue.

entries.name: No Magical Defenses
entries.summary: Gets no Magical Defense bonus from any hedge Art or Ability.
entries.description: The character's Arts and Abilities give him none of the Magical Defenses his tradition normally grants. Only for members of traditions that have such defenses.

entries.name: Expert Potion Brewer
entries.summary: The potion's Supernatural Ability counts double in its Lab Total.
entries.description: When the witch brews a potion, the Supernatural Ability it draws on counts twice in her Lab Total, raising the potion's Brew Potency.

entries.name: Flawed Folk Witch Gift Opening
entries.summary: One of the seven folk witch Abilities is not favored; learned later, it is at -1 to all totals.
entries.description: For a Gifted folk witch: one of the seven Abilities of the tradition was not opened. It is not favored and cannot be learned at character creation; if she learns it later, with the usual penalties for a new Supernatural Ability, all totals with it are at -1. May be taken once for each Ability.

entries.name: Flight
entries.summary: Grants Flight 1: fly through a fetish or a potion.
entries.description: The witch can fly, with the Supernatural Ability Flight 1.

entries.name: Folk Witch
entries.summary: Member of the folk witches: kitchen laboratory, folk witch magic and defenses, a coven; two seasons a year spent supporting herself.
entries.description: The folk witch's Social Status. She may do kitchen laboratory work, cast as a folk witch, has the tradition's Magical Defenses and belongs to a coven. She must spend two seasons a year supporting herself. Compatible with many other statuses, and with Wealthy and Poor.

entries.name: Harsh Moon
entries.summary: Suffers a Heavy Wound instead of a Medium one each month of a Witch Moon.
entries.description: When the witch undergoes a Witch Moon she suffers a Heavy Wound each month, rather than the usual Medium Wound.

entries.name: Healing
entries.summary: Grants Healing 1: true healing of wounds and Fatigue by incantation or potion.
entries.description: The witch can heal, with the Supernatural Ability Healing 1.

entries.name: Life-Linked Folk Witch Magic
entries.summary: +5 to a Casting Total for each Fatigue level spent.
entries.description: The witch may draw on her own vitality: each Fatigue level she spends when casting adds 5 to her Casting Total.

entries.name: Painless Moon
entries.summary: Suffers no Medium Wound during the months of a Witch Moon.
entries.description: The witch does not suffer the Medium Wound each month of a Witch Moon. Also called Painless Witch Moon.

entries.name: Poorly Trained Folk Witch
entries.summary: -50 xp from the folk witch apprenticeship.
entries.description: The witch's apprenticeship was poor: she has 50 fewer experience points from it.

entries.name: Primitive Tradition
entries.summary: Cannot brew potions.
entries.description: The witch's tradition does not know how to brew potions.

entries.name: Quick Charged Items
entries.summary: Makes a single-charge item in an hour per magnitude, up to their Lab Total.
entries.description: The magus can make single-use charged items: an effect of level up to their Lab Total takes one hour per magnitude and yields an item with one charge. All other rules for charged items apply (an Integration breakthrough from the cunning-folk).

entries.name: Rarefied Tradition
entries.summary: Uses her Abilities only through potions.
entries.description: The witch can use her Supernatural Abilities only by brewing them into potions.

entries.name: Ritual Items
entries.summary: Can make charged items with Ritual effects, each charge costing the Ritual's vis.
entries.description: The magus can make charged items with Ritual effects (an Integration breakthrough). Each charge needs as many pawns of vis as casting the effect would; the vis usable in a season and the number of charges are limited as usual.

entries.name: Secondary Insight (Runes)
entries.summary: Studying a rune gives 1 xp in every other rune of the same aett.
entries.description: When the vitki studies a rune, they also gain one experience point in each of the other runes of that aett. No rune gains more than one bonus point a season, and if they study runes from several aettir they choose which one gets the bonus.

entries.name: Sense of the Mystic
entries.summary: Their Intellego magical senses need not penetrate the sensed creature's Magic Resistance.
entries.description: Intellego effects with a Sense Target that this magus casts or invents need not penetrate the Magic Resistance of the creatures sensed, only that of the person granted the sense (an Integration breakthrough from Second Sight).

entries.name: Short-Ranged Curses
entries.summary: A curse fetish works only within 100 yards of its target; no effect on curse potions.
entries.description: The witch's curse fetishes work only while the target is within 100 yards: the curse takes effect when he comes in range, and an ongoing curse pauses when he leaves and must penetrate again when he returns. Curse potions are unaffected. Needs a Gifted folk witch or the Cursing Virtue.

entries.name: Silent Tradition
entries.summary: Has no incantation method.
entries.description: The witch's tradition has no incantations: she works only through fetishes and potions. Cannot be taken with Rarefied Tradition.

entries.name: Gruagach Blessing
entries.summary: Opens the gruagach Form Blessing (granting and removing good fortune) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the gruagach Form Blessing, the Art of granting and removing good fortune, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Gruagach Curse
entries.summary: Opens the gruagach Form Curse (curses and geasa) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the gruagach Form Curse, the Art of curses and geasa, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Gruagach Shape
entries.summary: Opens the gruagach Form Shape (transformation) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the gruagach Form Shape, the Art of transformation, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Gruagach Vision
entries.summary: Opens the gruagach Form Vision (illusions and visions) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the gruagach Form Vision, the Art of illusions and visions, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Gruagach Give
entries.summary: Opens the gruagach Technique Give (bestowing) at 0; a Difficult Art.
entries.description: Gives the gruagach Technique Give, the Art of bestowing, at 0. It is a Difficult Art, advancing on the Ability table, and is useless without a Form.

entries.name: Gruagach Take
entries.summary: Opens the gruagach Technique Take (removing) at 0; a Difficult Art.
entries.description: Gives the gruagach Technique Take, the Art of removing, at 0. It is a Difficult Art, advancing on the Ability table, and is useless without a Form.

entries.name: External Soul
entries.summary: Soul hidden in an object: physical injury cannot kill him and he does not age, but harm to the soul object kills him.
entries.description: Gained only by initiation. The gruagach's soul lives in an object outside his body. A wound that would kill or incapacitate him is split into lesser wounds instead, each time risking a Warping Point, and he no longer ages, gaining a Warping Point each year instead. Any damage to the soul object kills him. Irreversible.

entries.name: Fetch
entries.summary: An invisible animal companion with Second Sight 9 that warns of danger.
entries.description: The character has a fetch, an invisible animal companion with Second Sight 9 that warns him of danger, so that he is almost impossible to ambush. Also available to characters who are not gruagachan.

entries.name: Flexible Gruagach Magic
entries.summary: Varies Formulaic spells by up to 3 magnitudes instead of 2.
entries.description: When varying a Formulaic spell as he casts it, the gruagach may move its level by up to three magnitudes instead of two.

entries.name: Gruagach
entries.summary: Member of the gruagachan: gruagach laboratory work; must spend time supporting himself.
entries.description: The gruagach's Social Status. He may carry out the tradition's laboratory activities, and must spend time supporting himself as the core Social Status rules describe.

entries.name: Gruagach Master
entries.summary: Leads a collective of gruagachan and teaches students one season a year.
entries.description: The gruagach leads a collective and spends a season each year teaching students. If Poor he must also spend the normal time supporting himself; if Wealthy he has more or better students.

entries.name: Incompatible Hedge Arts
entries.summary: One Technique and Form pair he has cannot be used together.
entries.description: One combination of a Technique and a Form that the character has cannot be used. Taken by gruagachan and by learned magicians.

entries.name: Inflexible Magic
entries.summary: Varies Formulaic spells by only 1 magnitude.
entries.description: When varying a Formulaic spell as he casts it, the gruagach may move its level by only one magnitude.

entries.name: No Tattoo Magic
entries.summary: Cannot create or investigate tattoos.
entries.description: The gruagach cannot make magical tattoos or investigate them. Required of trollsynir and kolduni.

entries.name: Poorly Trained Gruagach
entries.summary: -50 xp on Arts and -25 spell levels from the apprenticeship.
entries.description: The gruagach's training was poor: 50 fewer experience points for Arts and 25 fewer levels of spells from his apprenticeship, though not below 0.

entries.name: Slow Caster (Runes)
entries.summary: Rune scripts take twice as long to carve; no single-round effects.
entries.description: The vitki's rune scripts take twice as long to carve. The vitki can never produce an effect in a single round, though they can manage a hasty spell in two rounds by taking the -15 penalty and leaving off their name and the description of the effect.

entries.name: Subtle Opening
entries.summary: Arts were Opened by a subtler method: no Arts penalty when learning Supernatural Abilities.
entries.description: The magus's Arts were Opened with a subtler technique learned by integrating the folk witches' Opening (an Integration breakthrough). The magus suffers no penalty to study Source Quality from their Arts when learning Supernatural Abilities, though other Supernatural Abilities still penalize them.

entries.name: Tattoo Mastery
entries.summary: Tattoos cost his Pictish score less in vis, but never below half the normal cost.
entries.description: The vis cost of the gruagach's tattoos is reduced by his Pictish score, but never below half the normal cost.

entries.name: Entreat the Powers
entries.summary: May call on any realm's powers to offset a negative realm-interaction modifier.
entries.description: The magician may call on the powers of any realm to offset a negative realm interaction: an Entreat Total (stress die + Presence + that realm's Lore) is added to a Casting Score or Lab Total, but never by more than the negative aura modifier, and it never helps reach the base total or Penetration. Granted by Opening to the learned magicians' tradition.

entries.name: Entreat the {realm} Powers
entries.summary: As Entreat the Powers, for one chosen realm.
entries.description: As Entreat the Powers, but the magician can call only on the powers of one chosen realm.

entries.name: Fortunam
entries.summary: Opens the learned magicians' Form Fortunam (luck) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the learned magicians' Form Fortunam, the Art of luck, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Magicam
entries.summary: Opens the learned magicians' Form Magicam (magic) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the learned magicians' Form Magicam, the Art of magic, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Salutem
entries.summary: Opens the learned magicians' Form Salutem (health) at 0.
entries.description: Gives the learned magicians' Form Salutem, the Art of health, at 0. It advances as a normal Art.

entries.name: Succurro
entries.summary: Opens the learned magicians' Technique Succurro (aid) at 0; a Difficult Art.
entries.description: Gives the learned magicians' Technique Succurro, the Art of aid, at 0. It is a Difficult Art, advancing on the Ability table.

entries.name: Intervention Prone
entries.summary: Rolls for Intervention on any botch.
entries.description: The magician must check for Intervention whenever he botches, not only when one botch brings two or more Warping Points.

entries.name: Laboratory Magician
entries.summary: Cannot memorise charms and casts only from texts; with No Text Casting, no charms at all.
entries.description: The magician cannot learn charms by heart and can cast only from a written text. With No Text Casting as well, he cannot cast charms at all. Required of mythic alchemists.

entries.name: Mathematicus of Bologna
entries.summary: Member of the learned magicians; needs a Technique and a Form, and a mundane Social Status as well.
entries.description: The learned magician's Social Status. He needs at least one Technique and one Form, and must also have a mundane Social Status such as Clerk, Magister in Artibus or Priest.

entries.name: Mythic Alchemy
entries.summary: Grants Mythic Alchemy 1: alchemy that truly transmutes matter.
entries.description: The character is a true alchemist, with the Supernatural Ability Mythic Alchemy 1. His reagents make permanent, non-magical changes to matter. Required of mythic alchemists.

entries.name: Mythic Herbalism
entries.summary: Grants Mythic Herbalism 1: brew concoctions that heal, poison or grant physical benefits.
entries.description: The character can brew concoctions from plants and other ingredients, with the Supernatural Ability Mythic Herbalism 1. Taught by the Pharmacopoeians; required of cunning-folk.

entries.name: Natural Magician
entries.summary: In a Divine or Infernal aura, adds Philosophiae to season-long magic work, capped by the negative aura modifier.
entries.description: For activities of a season or longer with a Magic Supernatural Ability in a Divine or Infernal aura, the character adds his Philosophiae to the Casting Total, Lab Total or roll, but never by more than the negative realm modifier. It never helps reach the base total or Penetration, and stacks with Entreat the Powers.

entries.name: No Chartae Making
entries.summary: Cannot make chartae.
entries.description: The magician cannot make chartae, the single-use charm devices.

entries.name: No Text Casting
entries.summary: Cannot cast charms from a text.
entries.description: The magician cannot cast a charm by reading it from a text, only from memory.

entries.name: Strong Amulet Magic
entries.summary: +10 to Lab Totals for amulets and chartae.
entries.description: The magician adds 10 to his Lab Total when making amulets and chartae.

entries.name: Strong Verbal Charms
entries.summary: Known charms are not halved; charms from a text are halved instead of divided by 5.
entries.description: A charm the magician knows by heart uses his full Casting Score plus the die, rather than half of it; a charm cast from a text is halved rather than divided by five.

entries.name: Skilled Master
entries.summary: +50 xp on Arts, Abilities and charms from the learned magician's training.
entries.description: The learned magician's master was skilled: 50 more experience points for Arts, Abilities and charms from his training.

entries.name: Poorly Trained Magician
entries.summary: -50 xp on Arts and charms from the learned magician's training.
entries.description: The learned magician's training was poor: 50 fewer experience points for Arts and charms, though not below 0.

entries.name: Half Taltós
entries.summary: A one-minute ritual gives Second Sight for a minute or a battle; his own weapons harm spirits.
entries.description: A one-minute ritual gives the character Second Sight for a minute or for one battle; each use costs a Fatigue level unless he makes an Athletics + Stamina roll against 6. His own weapons can harm spirits, and a new one takes a month to attune. Grogs may take it.

entries.name: Hamr
entries.summary: A trance near a battlefield sends out an animal-shaped phantasticum; needs a prop.
entries.description: In a trance near a battlefield the character sends out a corporeal, animal-shaped phantasticum. He needs a prop such as a hide or a drug, and has none of the other nightwalker powers.

entries.name: Nightwalker
entries.summary: Strays from the body while insensible as a phantasticum, and can lead others astray.
entries.description: While his body lies insensible, the nightwalker's spirit strays as a phantasticum, tangible or not, in human, animal or elemental form, and can lead others' spirits with it. He has Second Sight 1, usable only in phantastic form, and can harm spirits while intangible. His body appears dead and is vulnerable, and injuries to the phantasticum reflect on it.

entries.name: Sleepwalker
entries.summary: Fights cloaked in a larger hybrid phantasticum; cannot stray.
entries.description: The character fights cloaked in a larger, hybrid phantasticum, but cannot stray and lacks nearly all other nightwalker powers. He needs props.

entries.name: Major Magical Deficiency
entries.summary: Casting Total halved for scripts with any rune of one aett, or three chosen runes unusable.
entries.description: Either the vitki's Casting Total is halved for any script containing a rune of one aett, or he cannot use three chosen runes at all.

entries.name: Minor Magical Deficiency
entries.summary: Casting Total halved for scripts with any of three runes, or one rune unusable.
entries.description: Either the vitki's Casting Total is halved for any script containing one of three chosen runes, or he cannot use one chosen rune at all. A student whose master is below 2 in a rune gains this Flaw for it.

entries.name: Major Rune Focus
entries.summary: Double the rune score for effects of one focus inscribed in its material.
entries.description: For effects of the chosen kind inscribed in its material, the vitki doubles the rune score he uses: Victory on metal weapons and armour, Ale on horn, leather or his own fingernails, Fertility on coins and jewellery, Sea on ships, carts and sails, Healing on bone, Speech on wood, Wisdom on stone, Strength on flesh. Only one focus at character creation.

entries.name: Minor Rune Focus
entries.summary: As Major Rune Focus, for one chosen rune.
entries.description: As Major Rune Focus, but for one chosen rune, used as the target rune or the effect rune.

entries.name: Mastered Rune
entries.summary: Scripts with one rune: 3 fewer botch dice and casting penalties halved.
entries.description: For scripts using the chosen rune the vitki rolls three fewer botch dice (at least one) and all casting penalties are halved. May be taken once for each rune.

entries.name: Nameless Runes
entries.summary: No penalty for omitting his name from a script.
entries.description: The vitki suffers no penalty for leaving his name off a script, though he gains no bonus for including it. The runes still link to him magically.

entries.name: Nátt-thel Prone
entries.summary: Checks for Nátt-thel on any single botch.
entries.description: The vitki must check for Nátt-thel whenever he botches, not only when one botch brings two or more Warping Points. A student Opened by a master in or lost to Nátt-thel gains this Flaw.

entries.name: Secret Runes
entries.summary: Hidden description costs no penalty and no description only -5; taken twice, no penalty at all.
entries.description: Hiding a script's description costs the vitki no penalty, and omitting it only -5, but he gains no bonus for a normal inscription (the emphasis bonus still applies). Taken twice, there is no penalty at all.

entries.name: Short-Lived Runes
entries.summary: Rune effects are not permanent: each lasts a secretly rolled time.
entries.description: The vitki's effects are not permanent: for each one the storyguide secretly rolls on the Nátt-thel Duration chart, adding one for each pawn of vis or Confidence Point spent in casting. The Flaw's own entry (p. 123) calls it Major; the Vitkar Flaws list on the same page shows it as Minor.

entries.name: The Enigma
entries.summary: Initiated into the Outer Mystery of The Enigma; Enigmatic Wisdom 1.
entries.description: You have been initiated into the Outer Mystery of The Enigma (see page 235), and thus are a member of House Criamon. You have a score of 1 in Enigmatic Wisdom. Note that all Criamon magi get this Virtue free at character creation.

entries.name: Enticer of Multitudes
entries.summary: Incite groups toward a chosen sin: members roll that Personality Trait at +5 or more; cannot control the resulting frenzy.
entries.description: The character has a version of the Inspirational Virtue that can only be used to manipulate people toward evil acts. The character appears demagogic rather than heroic, and cannot control a group once he has whipped it into a frenzy. The enticer forces individuals in a group to make Personality Trait rolls for the particular sin they are attempting to evoke, with a bonus of +5 or more.

entries.name: Entrancement
entries.summary: Control another's will by eye contact and a spoken command; grants Entrancement 1.
entries.description: You have the power to control another's will by staring into their eyes and giving them a verbal command. Choosing this Virtue confers the Ability Entrancement 1 (page 164).

entries.name: Essential Virtue
entries.summary: One beneficial Essential Trait: +3 (Minor) or +6 (Major), boosting a Characteristic in situations or an unalterable Personality Trait.
entries.description: The character receives one generally beneficial Essential Trait at either +3 for Minor or +6 for Major, which either positively affects rolls associated with a particular Characteristic in certain situations, like Intuitive +3 or Good Aim +6, or gives the character a beneficial Personality Trait that is part of its essential nature and cannot be influenced by magic (see Essential Traits, below). _ You can take this Virtue more than once, so long as you choose a different Essential Trait each time.

entries.name: Essential Virtue
entries.summary: One beneficial Essential Trait: +3 (Minor) or +6 (Major), boosting a Characteristic in situations or an unalterable Personality Trait.
entries.description: The character receives one generally beneficial Essential Trait at either +3 for Minor or +6 for Major, which either positively affects rolls associated with a particular Characteristic in certain situations, like Intuitive +3 or Good Aim +6, or gives the character a beneficial Personality Trait that is part of its essential nature and cannot be influenced by magic (see Essential Traits, below). _ You can take this Virtue more than once, so long as you choose a different Essential Trait each time.

entries.name: Eunuch
entries.summary: Educated Byzantine courtier, steward or scribe; Academic Abilities at character creation.
entries.description: You have been educated and trained to serve the Byzantine nobility as a courtier, steward, chamberlain, scribe, lawyer, or accountant. You are likely employed by a court, a lesser noble, or a covenant. It is also possible for you to pursue a career in the eastern Church, and some monasteries accept eunuchs. Due to your education, you may take Academic Abilities during character creation. This Virtue is only available to male characters, who must be sexually incapable, rather than simply inactive. This may be due to castration (see the Castratus Flaw), but need not be.

entries.name: Evocation
entries.summary: Grants Evocation at 1: Communication-based rites invoking faerie gods for a Warping or Confidence point; can use vis (+2 per pawn).
entries.description: See Chapter 6: Faerie Wizardry for a full description of this Faerie Method. Choosing this Virtue gives the character Evocation with an initial score of 1.

entries.name: Exotic Casting
entries.summary: Casts Hermetic spells by non-Hermetic methods; others identify the Form at Ease Factor 15, not reduced by magnitude.
entries.description: The magus uses non-Hermetic methods to cast Hermetic spells. While he still needs to employ obvious ritual actions, these are not the same words and gestures taught as part of Magic Theory within the Order, and other magi who are unfamiliar with the magus's tradition find it very hard to recognize which spell he is casting. Any attempt to determine the Form of his magical effect (page 217) is made against an Ease Factor of 15, without the magnitude of the effect being subtracted from this Ease Factor as normal. If the character has any Supernatural Abilities, then he uses the same methods to cast his Hermetic magic as he does to use his non-Hermetic magic. The magus cannot choose to use the standard Hermetic methods instead of those of his native tradition, but can choose to reduce or forgo words and gestures in the usual fashion (page 216).

entries.name: External Vis
entries.summary: Its anchor (vis) sits in a role prop that can be far from its body; Major: the prop also grants its bearer one Minor Virtue.
entries.description: The faerie's spiritual essence (anchor) resides in one of the props traditional for its role, and this can be carried far from the faerie's body without the faerie suffering ill effects. There is an Arcane Connection between the object containing the faerie's spiritual essence and the faerie's body. If this connection is broken, or if the object is destroyed, the faerie's distant body disintegrates, but the essence can construct a new body, given sufficient time. If the vis in the prop is used, the faerie is permanently destroyed. When selected as a Major Virtue, the prop provides its bearer with any one Minor Virtue, selected at creation. This provides the faerie with a little additional power, but its main advantage is that humans who discover the object are far more likely to treasure it, and keep it safe. This provides the faerie with time to form a new physical body and reclaim his object. As an example, a faerie warrior with a Might of 20 uses his sword as his spiritual anchor. A character that defeats the warrior finds that the sword contains 4 pawns of vis, but also finds that the sword has no Encumbrance and grants a human wielder a +2 bonus on the Single Weapon Ability. The bonus comes from the Grant Puissance power, described later. If the human keeps the weapon, then eventually the faerie can generate a fresh body, and seek out the wielder and challenge him to a duel.

entries.name: External Vis
entries.summary: Its anchor (vis) sits in a role prop that can be far from its body; Major: the prop also grants its bearer one Minor Virtue.
entries.description: The faerie's spiritual essence (anchor) resides in one of the props traditional for its role, and this can be carried far from the faerie's body without the faerie suffering ill effects. There is an Arcane Connection between the object containing the faerie's spiritual essence and the faerie's body. If this connection is broken, or if the object is destroyed, the faerie's distant body disintegrates, but the essence can construct a new body, given sufficient time. If the vis in the prop is used, the faerie is permanently destroyed. When selected as a Major Virtue, the prop provides its bearer with any one Minor Virtue, selected at creation. This provides the faerie with a little additional power, but its main advantage is that humans who discover the object are far more likely to treasure it, and keep it safe. This provides the faerie with time to form a new physical body and reclaim his object. As an example, a faerie warrior with a Might of 20 uses his sword as his spiritual anchor. A character that defeats the warrior finds that the sword contains 4 pawns of vis, but also finds that the sword has no Encumbrance and grants a human wielder a +2 bonus on the Single Weapon Ability. The bonus comes from the Grant Puissance power, described later. If the human keeps the weapon, then eventually the faerie can generate a fresh body, and seek out the wielder and challenge him to a duel.

entries.name: Extractor of {form} Vis
entries.summary: Extract (Form) vis in the lab from a Magic aura exemplifying that Form: pawns = CrVi (Form) Lab Total / 10, round up.
entries.description: The magus can extract (Form) vis from a Magic aura, but only if the features of the aura exemplify the Form. For example, an aura on the shores of a lake might exemplify Aquam, an aura at a burial-site exemplifies Corpus, etc. Extracting vis in this way is a Laboratory activity; the magus extracts a number of pawns of Vis equal to a tenth of his Creo Vim (Form) Lab Total (round up). Obviously, he needs to have a Laboratory in the aura too, and, of course, the magus can chose to extract Vim vis instead (see page 250). This Virtue may be taken multiple times (once for each Form).

entries.name: Eye of Hephaestus
entries.summary: Senses flaws in crafted items by touch; Per + Awareness vs 9 reveals supernatural items' powers, vs 12 detects Hermetic enchantment.
entries.description: The character can innately tell the quality of a manufactured item. If the item is somehow flawed he is instantly aware of that by merely touching it. He also has a chance to tell if an item is magical. For supernatural items made by a craftsman, make a Perception + Awareness + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9. If successful, the character knows the power of the item. For Hermetic enchanted items, or those made by other sorcerers, make a Perception + Awareness + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12. If successful, the character knows the item is enchanted, but has no idea how, or what its powers might be. Botching either roll results in false information. This Virtue does not offer any information about the actions or commands necessary to trigger an item's powers. Hephaestus was a pagan god of craftsmen, primarily metallurgists. Calling this Virtue the Eye of St Dunstan is more appropriate for Christian characters.

entries.name: Eyes of Theseus
entries.summary: While concentrating, an illusory string leads to any object in the room able to make a known person express vitality, often revealing secrets.
entries.description: When the initiate concentrates, this Virtue creates an illusionary string, which leads away from the initiate to any object in the room that has the power to cause a known human to express vitality. Vitality, which faeries crave, is expressed in heightened states of emotion, or when phases of life come to an end. This means that the string will often lead to objects which are linked to the secrets of nearby people. These secrets do not necessarily have anything to do with the crime the initiate is investigating, however. (Minor Virtue 18 = Mystagogue (9) + Special time and place (3) + Sacrifice of talisman (or something of equal value to a non-magus) +6: A clew is a ball of string. Theseus used a ball of string to lead him out of the labyrinth of Knossos. Initiates to this degree are expected to have clews as their talismans. Kabeiros has not yet developed a way to translate this bit of glamour for non-magi.)

entries.name: Fabric Ripper
entries.summary: 1 Fatigue level per object: tear any plant- or animal-fibre item by will (PeAn(He) 25, Penetration +0, no words or gestures).
entries.description: The character has the supernatural ability to tear any manufactured thing made from plant or animal fibers. This allows her to destroy sails, break the strap holding on individual pieces of armor, snap the tack of a horse, burst a sack, and tatter a pair of pants with her mind. She spends a Fatigue level to activate the ability, and may only target one object per Fatigue level spent. This is a PeAn(He) 25 effect with +0 Penetration, and does not require any words or gestures. Community Gloss This virtue is associated with a minor hedge tradition concentrated in the area of Tunis, as described in Between Sand & Sea, Chapter Four.

entries.name: Factor
entries.summary: Manages a trading house's interests in one city, with strong social position and far-flung connections.
entries.description: The character manages the interests of a trading house in a single city. This gives the character a strong social position and connections to many other regions; see City and Guild for more details. Many factors are junior partners in their companies, and they choose the Partner Virtue, not this one.

entries.name: Faerie Background
entries.summary: Two Sympathy Traits (one positive, one negative) starting at the Warping Score; may freely raise Warping Score at creation.
entries.description: Due to something unusual about the character's birth or childhood, the character has a strong resonance with one aspect of the faerie realm. It grants the character two Sympathy Traits, one positive and the other negative, with initial values equal to the character's Warping Score. These Traits should be appropriate to the character's faerie background; for example, a character raised by faerie wolves might have Fear (positive) and Courage (negative) Sympathy Traits, perhaps to represent wolves' love of causing fear and their tendency to back down when challenged. See the Faerie Sympathy Virtue and Faerie Antipathy Flaw, below, for information about how these Traits increase and decrease. Players with this Virtue may freely increase their character's Warping Score during character creation, though they should have some idea of what in the character's past caused this Warping to occur. This Virtue is especially appropriate for characters who have the Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood Virtues, or the Faerie Upbringing Flaw; see the expanded descriptions of the different types of Faerie Blood, earlier, for suggested Sympathy Traits.

entries.name: Faerie Beast
entries.summary: Has an animal-form faerie body with all faerie-body advantages; animal-form limits (no hands, no speech) cannot be taken as Flaws.
entries.description: The character appears to be an animal. It has all of the advantages of being a faerie, and having a faerie body. The innate limitations of an animal form, such as having no hands and being unable to pronounce human words, may not be taken as Flaws. Faerie beasts that wish to speak like humans may take Language Pretenses, or the Faerie Speech Virtue.

entries.name: Faerie Blood
entries.summary: -1 aging rolls, faeries at ease, Faerie Lore at creation; plus one blood type's perk, e.g. Dwarf +1 Craft, Sidhe +1 Presence (max +3).
entries.description: Somewhere in your ancestry there is a faerie, and this relation gives you an intuitive grasp of the motivations and personalities of those supernatural folk. Faeries are more comfortable around you than around other humans, and given time, may even forget the mortal blood in your veins. You are resistant to aging, and get -1 to all aging rolls. Type of Faerie Blood (pick one, or create a similar one): Blood of the Bee King: The descendants of Bee Kings may give simple instructions to bees they touch, and may understand the thoughts dominating hives of bees. They are unable to give bees instructions that will kill them, except to command warrior bees to attack, since warrior bees are so willing to die. (Penetration 25) Dwarf Blood: You are descended from the master craftsmen of the fay, and get a +1 bonus to any total including a Craft Ability. Goblin Blood: Your ancestors were the sneaky inhabitants of the shadows underground, and you get a +1 bonus on all totals involving stealth. Satyr Blood: The satyrs are notoriously lecherous. You get a +1 bonus to Communication and Presence totals when dealing with sexually compatible characters. Sidhe Blood: You are descended from one of the noble fay who rule the lands of Summer and sunlight. Because of the striking and unusual qualities of your nature add +1 to your Presence, but not to more than +3. Many mortals may consider you fascinating or alluring. Spinnen Blood: A character who has Spinnen Blood can convert his or her own body weight of fiber into cloth per day, simply by touching it. Old cloth, or products made of cloth fibers, can be unwoven using the same ability, but this counts toward the maximum weight of cloth a character can alter per day. Some Spinnen, particularly those who have served as companions to magi, create other useful objects, like tents, ropes, or sails in lieu of the same weight of cloth. These characters are from a single family line that originated near Ghent; see The Lion and the Lily, page 97, for details of how most of the family live. Undine Blood: The undines are the faeries of the water, and you get a +2 bonus to any action taken underwater, which will partially offset any penalty applied. Characters with Faerie Blood can learn Faerie Lore at character generation.

entries.name: Faerie Blood (Bloodcap)
entries.summary: Descended from a cruel winter faerie: +1 Strength (max +3); long teeth and nails, looks older; very susceptible to the Divine.
entries.description: You are descended from a frightening spirit of cruel, dark winter, and receive a +1 bonus to your Strength, though this does not increase your score beyond +3. Your teeth and nails tend to be much longer than normal and you look older than you actually are. You also tend to be very susceptible to the Divine, and should_ take a Flaw to represent that fact. This faerie lineage is rare in humans, and probably found only in characters of House Mercere.

entries.name: Faerie Blood (Jentil)
entries.summary: Descended from the Basque giants: -1 to Aging rolls, +1 to recovery rolls, +1 Strength (max +3); compatible with Large and Giant Blood.
entries.description: Your family traces itself to the Jentilak, the giants who held the Basque lands before men, raised great stone monuments, and taught smithing and farming before they all but vanished. As a Minor Virtue you age more slowly (+1 against aging), recover better (+1 to recovery rolls) and gain +1 Strength, which cannot take it above +3. You may also have Large or Giant Blood.

entries.name: Faerie Blood (Jentil)
entries.summary: Strong Jentil blood: +1 Strength (max +3), +1 Size, Second Sight, -3 to Aging rolls and none before 50; a giant's looks give you away.
entries.description: Your family traces itself to the Jentilak, the giants who held the Basque lands before men, raised great stone monuments, and taught smithing and farming before they all but vanished. As a Major Virtue you keep the Minor version's +1 Strength (to at most +3), but in place of its recovery bonus you gain +1 Size; you also have Second Sight, a +3 bonus against aging, and make no aging rolls until you are 50. Something in your build betrays the giant ancestry, such as huge hands and feet or heavy, outsized features. You may also have Large or Giant Blood.

entries.name: Faerie Blood (Laminak)
entries.summary: Descended from Basque river faeries: +1 Stamina or +1 Presence (max +3); people find you oddly fascinating; your toes are webbed.
entries.description: One of your forebears was a lamia, one of the river faeries of the Basque Country, known both for their tireless work and for their beauty. Take after one side or the other: +1 to Stamina or +1 to Presence, in either case to no more than +3. Folk are drawn to you without knowing why. Your toes are joined by webs of skin.

entries.name: Faerie Blood (Spinnen)
entries.summary: Each day, turn up to your own body weight of fiber into cloth (or tents, ropes, sails) by touch, or unweave cloth within that limit.
entries.description: A character who has Spinnen Blood can convert his or her own body weight of fiber into cloth per day, simply by touching it. Old cloth, or products made of cloth fibers, can be unwoven using the same ability, but this counts toward the maximum weight of cloth a character can alter per day. Some Spinnen, particularly those who have served as companions to magi, create other useful objects, like tents, ropes, or sails in lieu of the same weight of cloth.

entries.name: Faerie Doctor
entries.summary: Makes the character a Faerie Doctor Mythic Companion and grants Dowsing free.
entries.description: This Virtue makes you a Faerie Doctor and a Mythic Companion (page 63). You get the Dowsing Virtue for free.

entries.name: Faerie Instructor
entries.summary: Can take human Abilities in bargains, store them, and pass them to favored humans by trading them for the student's current Ability.
entries.description: Some faeries have the ability to take human Abilities when striking bargains. If the faerie has this Virtue, these Abilities can be stored, then given to favored humans. The faerie imparts the Ability by trading it for the Ability that the student currently has. It does this either by giving the human a prop and claiming it is a magic item, which allows the faerie to easily trade the Abilities back when the story is over, or by pretending to teach the human. Human teachers know that faeries are faking, because their training is too swift to be natural, and too similar to mystery initiation to be effective. It focuses on the trainee reaching an appropriate mental state, rather than the repetitive practice required for real learning.

entries.name: Faerie Legacy
entries.summary: Replaces its Faerie Blood variety's benefit with the stronger Legacy version (e.g. Sidhe: Presence +1, up to +4).
entries.description: This Virtue can only be taken by characters with Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood. Your Faerie Blood is particularly potent, and the usual benefit deriving from it is replaced with a more powerful version. See Varieties of Faerie Blood (earlier) for details on how the benefit is affected. Note that the legacy benefit from this Virtue is instead of the normal benefit, not in addition to it.

entries.name: Faerie Magic
entries.summary: Initiated into the Outer Mystery of Faerie Magic; Faerie Magic 1.
entries.description: You have been initiated into the Outer Mystery of Faerie Magic (see page 236), and thus are a member of House Merinita. You have the Ability Faerie Magic 1. Note that all Merinita magi gain this Virtue for free at character generation.

entries.name: Faerie Sight
entries.summary: Constant, free: tells glamour from mundane, sees glamour ownership and Arcane Connections, reads and sees through glamour (Awareness rolls).
entries.description: This Virtue, which works constantly at no cost to the faerie, is used in conjunction with the Awareness Pretense. It allows faeries to: Tell mundane from glamourous things. (Automatic success: no roll required.) See the borders of glamour, so that they know which faerie that props and territories belong to. (Automatic success: no roll required.) See Arcane Connections, so that they know which objects belong to a human (automatic success), and also to which human they belong. (If human and object can be observed, automatic success.) Read each other's glamour. Faerie Lore is a body of knowledge that humans learn through experience, so very few faeries have it. (Ease Factor = Might of other faerie/5) Faeries use the ability to read each other's glamour to guide their interactions, instead of using Faerie Lore. See mundane things hidden by glamour. (Ease Factor = 3 + (Might of Faerie causing the glamour - Might of the faerie attempting to see through the glamour)/5)

entries.name: Faerie Speech
entries.summary: Speaks whatever language its audience uses, at no Might cost and not magically resisted.
entries.description: Many faeries have a Pretense called Faerie Speech, which they use instead of acquiring human languages. Faeries seem to know the same languages as whomever they are talking to. If speaking to a group that has demonstrated mixed linguistic skills, the faerie may select which language to speak in. This effect occurs whenever the faerie speaks and costs no Might. It is not magically resisted, because the effect only alters the behavior of the faerie. If the faerie has not heard a person from its audience speak, it may only use whichever language it last used with humans. Once its audience speaks, the faerie may then converse in the correct language for its audience. In the bestiary chapter, Faerie Speech is frequently given to characters designed as NPCs. Characters designed for possible use by players have this Virtue more rarely, to free up a Virtue slot, but it is still appropriate for a wide variety of faeries.

entries.name: (Faerie) Summoning
entries.summary: Grants Summoning at 0: call a faerie of Might up to Sympathy Traits x 5 to bargain; binds and wards if total beats its Might.
entries.description: See Chapter 6: Faerie Wizardry for a full description. Choosing this Virtue gives the character Summoning with an initial score of 0.

entries.name: Faerie Sympathy
entries.summary: One positive Sympathy Trait at +3 (Major) or +1 (Minor), improvable to initial value + Warping Score; may raise Warping at creation.
entries.description: The character receives a positive Sympathy Trait. As a Major Virtue, this has an initial score of +3; as a Minor Virtue it is +1. This Trait may be increased with experience points, up to a maximum score of (the initial value + the character's Warping Score). For example, a character with Warping Score 1 and the Major Virtue could begin with a +4 Trait. Players with this Virtue may freely increase their character's Warping Score during character creation, though they should have some idea of what in the character's past caused this Warping to occur. This Virtue may be taken more than once. See Sympathy, earlier, for more information about Sympathy Traits.

entries.name: Faerie Sympathy
entries.summary: One positive Sympathy Trait at +3 (Major) or +1 (Minor), improvable to initial value + Warping Score; may raise Warping at creation.
entries.description: The character receives a positive Sympathy Trait. As a Major Virtue, this has an initial score of +3; as a Minor Virtue it is +1. This Trait may be increased with experience points, up to a maximum score of (the initial value + the character's Warping Score). For example, a character with Warping Score 1 and the Major Virtue could begin with a +4 Trait. Players with this Virtue may freely increase their character's Warping Score during character creation, though they should have some idea of what in the character's past caused this Warping to occur. This Virtue may be taken more than once. See Sympathy, earlier, for more information about Sympathy Traits.

entries.name: Faerie Trainer
entries.summary: Has real human Abilities rather than Pretenses, so can train humans conventionally until it advances them as Pretenses.
entries.description: The character has one or more human Abilities, rather than Pretenses, and so it may train humans using conventional methods. The faerie can develop these abilities further using human methods, or can convert them to Pretenses and increase them as a faerie would. Once an Ability has been advanced as a Pretense, the maximum level at which the faerie can train humans has been reached.

entries.name: Faerie-Raised Magic
entries.summary: Invent spells mimicking observed supernatural effects using Exposure, Adventure or Practice xp (magnitude + 4 xp each); includes Spell Improvisation.
entries.description: The character's experience with faeries and the Faerie realm has conditioned him to invent spells very quickly; to him, Formulaic spells seem like inherent powers that you can learn through observation and experimentation. Because of this, he can teach himself spells outside of the laboratory. You may spend experience points from Exposure, Adventure, and Practice on spells you could normally invent that mimic faerie powers or other supernatural effects your character has observed that season. To invent a spell in this way, the magus's Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory must at least equal (the spell's level - 10), and you must spend a number of experience points equal to (the spell magnitude + 4). Spells of level 5 or less cost their level in experience points (but always at least 1). For example, a level 2 spell costs 2 experience points, and a Level 15 spell costs 7 experience points. The magus cannot invent Ritual spells in this way. If the magus already knows a spell that is similar to one he wishes to invent (see Similar Spells, page 260), any experience points you spend towards learning that spell are increased by one-half, rounded up. This means that a level 25 spell would cost 6 experience points instead of 9, for example. This Virtue also includes the Virtue Spell Improvisation. That is, you may add the magnitude of a known Formulaic spell as a bonus to your character's Casting Total when spontaneously casting a spell that is similar to it. If you take this Virtue during character creation, you should normally take the Faerie Upbringing Flaw. Because the magus's master also had to teach him about human society, he probably had less time to teach him Hermetic magic. It is possible that the apprentice invented Formulaic spells quickly enough on his own to compensate for this, but you might take the Weak Parens Flaw to suggest this limitation of his apprenticeship.

entries.name: Failed Apprentice
entries.summary: Former apprentice; may learn Academic, Arcane and Martial Abilities at creation; may retain Supernatural Abilities.
entries.description: You were once apprenticed to a mage, but something kept you from completing your studies. Perhaps your Gift was incomplete or some grievous mishap robbed you of it altogether. You may still work for your former master or for the covenant in some other capacity. Magi welcome you and have compassion for you -- those who are given to such emotions, anyway. You may learn Academic, Arcane, and Martial Abilities during character creation, and you are familiar with the lives of magi. You may not have The Gift, but if your Gift was not completely destroyed, you may have some Supernatural Abilities. The Wealthy Virtue and Poor Flaw affect you normally.

entries.name: Falconer
entries.summary: Trains a patron's hawks; +50 xp for Animal Handling, Area Lore, Etiquette, Hunt, Latin, Profession: Falconer, Ride.
entries.description: The character trains hawks and falcons for a noble patron, and is responsible for the training, breeding, and health of the animals. He often has a personal servant to assist, and is an important member of the noble household, treated with great respect. He should possess the Ability Profession: Falconer, which governs the care of the birds, treatment of their diseases, and acquisition and breeding of hawks and falcons. The Ability Animal Handling is used for the training of the hawks. A specialist in non-falcons, such as the hawks, is called an austringer. A falconer receives 50 extra experience points at character generation to spend on the Abilities Animal Handling, Area Lore, Etiquette, Hunt, Latin, Profession: Falconer, and Ride. Many falconers are also Educated.

entries.name: Falls Like a Cat
entries.summary: No injury from falls up to 3x own height (6x if softened); beyond, +1 Impact per extra foot (hard) or four feet (soft).
entries.description: The character is not injured by falls of up to three times his height, or six times his height if he can soften his fall by catching on windowsills, breaking through awnings, or hitting branches on the way down. At greater heights the character suffers Impact damage of +1 for every additional foot, if landing on a hard surface, or for every additional four feet, if landing on a soft surface.

entries.name: The False Gift
entries.summary: Hell-corrupted Gift: all The Gift's benefits and penalties, but Vituperation replaces Twilight and its Powers read unholy; lost on absolution.
entries.description: The Infernal has the ability to corrupt and impersonate the Powers of other realms, and one of the most insidious applications is for characters who have a version of The Gift that is not like that of other characters, but rather has been thoroughly corrupted by Infernal powers. This "False Gift" includes all the benefits and penalties of the magical version: the character suffers mistrust, suspicion, and envy among the mundane populace, and while he may learn magical Supernatural Abilities, because of his association with the Infernal realm these are actually False Powers that always appear unholy to Divine or Infernal Powers of investigation. When exposed to Warping, instead of experiencing Twilight, a character with the False Gift must undergo Vituperation. If the character should ever confess the nature of his Gift and accept spiritual absolution, allowing his soul to be cleansed of sin and exorcising the Infernal influences that corrupted his very nature, he loses The Gift completely. This also prevents him from using any Supernatural Abilities that he has learned with The Gift, including the Hermetic Arts. False magic is a tragic thing to possess, because once the character realizes the Infernal nature of his powers, he may decide that using them for any reason is a form of infernalism. Yet very few people would choose to give up their powers if placed in a similar position, and perhaps the character can justify the stain of his sins as a sort of unpleasant side effect of his Gift: damned by association with the Infernal realm, but not actually evil. This is a fascinating and tragic journey to roleplay, as the character must slowly accept that the thing that almost entirely defines him as a person in Mythic Europe is a lie. The False Gift has no cost, like its magical counterpart, though it requires the False Power Flaw (see Chapter 9: Infernal Characters). If the character is not a magus, he may also begin with one free Supernatural Ability as normal, but this is automatically another False Power, and he does not take the False Power Flaw again to modify it.

entries.name: Familiarity with the Fae
entries.summary: +2 to social rolls with faeries, Common Sense regarding faeries, and Faerie Lore at character creation.
entries.description: You have a natural understanding of faerie ways, perhaps due to spending time among them. You get a +2 to all rolls involving social interaction with faeries. You also gain the effects of the Common Sense Virtue, but only when the situation pertains to faeries. You may purchase Faerie Lore at character generation, even if normally unable to take Arcane Abilities.

entries.name: Famous
entries.summary: Good Reputation 4 of your choice and type.
entries.description: You have a good Reputation of level 4. Choose any reputation you like (it need not be justified), and one type.

entries.name: Fast Caster
entries.summary: +3 Initiative to cast spells in combat and +3 to fast-casting speed rolls.
entries.description: Your magic takes less time to perform than that of other magi. You gain +3 to Initiative to cast spells in combat and +3 to rolls to determine fast casting speed.

entries.name: Fast Might Recovery
entries.summary: Recovers its entire Might pool in six hours instead of 24.
entries.description: This Virtue allows faeries to recover spent Might in a quarter of the normal time. Instead of completely refreshing its Might over the course of 24 hours, the character restores its entire Might Pool in only six hours.

entries.name: Feast of the Dead
entries.summary: Regains 2 lost Might after draining a Long-Term Fatigue level from, or causing at least a Medium Wound to, a human.
entries.description: This Virtue allows a faerie to recover 2 lost Might after draining a Long Term Fatigue Level from, or causing at least a Medium Wound to, a human. Different fairies employ various methods to extract vitality from humans. This Virtue does not, of itself, cause damage. For example, a faerie that feeds on the blood of sleeping shepherds must make a successful Bite attack to drink sufficient blood from a sleeping shepherd to cause the loss of a Long Term Fatigue Level. The faerie's player can then claim 2 lost Might points.

entries.name: Feast of the Fae
entries.summary: Once per day, regains 5 lost Might by receiving a traditional human offering (food left out, or even wards for dark faeries).
entries.description: This Virtue allows a faerie to recover 5 lost Might by receiving traditional sacrifices left from a human. Sacrifices include food left on doorsteps for the faerie to consume, but some dark faeries feed on the wards left to keep them at bay, accepting them as the price that humans pay for safety. This power can only be used once per day.

entries.name: Feather Messenger
entries.summary: Detach a feather and telepathically write with it as an inkless quill while within Sight.
entries.description: This Virtue is only available to a character who can take the form of a bird (which may be her natural form). She can painlessly separate a feather from her body, and use it to write as a quill, controlling its movements telepathically while it remains within Sight. The quill doesn't need ink; it provides it magically. After she finishes writing, the character can reattach the feather if in bird form. The quality of the character as a scribe does not differ between human and bird forms. The character can also pull off feathers in bird form, turn into a human, and still mentally control the dropped feathers. This Virtue is particularly associated with a north African magical tradition called the Daughters of Four Fathers (see Between Sand & Sea, page 107).

entries.name: Fector
entries.summary: Gifted hunter Opened to the Hunters' Arts: has all three Practice Arts (Scry, Ban, Slay), three Foe Arts, and Second Sight free.
entries.description: A Fector character takes the place of a player's magus character. They have both The Gift and the free Fector Social Status Virtue; the latter is akin to Hermetic Magus, and represents the fact that the character has been Opened to the Hunters' Arts. A Fector has all three Practice Arts of Scry, Ban, and Slay, and can choose three Foe Arts. The character is Opened to these hedge Arts (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, page 7) using his master's Intelligence + Scry total. Currently, the Fectores only know the Foe Arts of Vampire, Werewolf, Ghost, Nightwalker, and Witch, but are working to integrate other Foes. A Fector also has the Second Sight Virtue at no cost. They are usually apprenticed to a Fector around adolescence, and training takes five years. During this time, the Fector receives 120 experience points that can be spent on the Hunters' Arts or on Abilities. A Fector can take Martial and Arcane Abilities at Character Creation, as well as Latin, but a Virtue is required to take any other Academic Abilities. The Fectores, unlike many other hedge traditions, do not have Magical Defenses except for those granted by the Ban Art. However, Fectores who are members of the Order (that is, most of them) can be taught the Parma Magica.

entries.name: Feminine Ceremony
entries.summary: A Matres & Matrones form of the Ceremony Ability, used for group casting; named in a stat block only, so it follows Ceremony's rules.
entries.description: The Matres and Matrones' own version of Ceremony, which lets the character lead a group of participants in a joint casting. The book gives it only as a Major Virtue and an Ability (used for group casting) in the statistics of the cult's founder, with no rules of its own; treat it as the Ceremony Virtue and Ability, practised among the cult's women.

entries.name: The Feminine Gift
entries.summary: Matres & Matrones Initiation: your Gift acts as the Gentle Gift toward women and the Blatant Gift toward men; others react as usual.
entries.description: A Mystery of the Matres and Matrones, open to a character who already has the normal Gift. Human women respond to her as if she had the Gentle Gift, while human men respond as if she had the Blatant Gift, and need as long to grow used to her as they would to a Blatant magus. Animals, beings with Might and everyone else meet her ordinary Gift. Printed as either a Hermetic or a Supernatural Virtue.

entries.name: Feminine Sympathy
entries.summary: Feminine Sympathy Trait +1 (Major: +3), added like a specialty to mundane Ability rolls that act directly on a woman; such rolls use stress dice.
entries.description: Initiated by the second level of the Matres and Matrones. The character gains a Sympathy Trait, Feminine Sympathy, at +1 for the Minor Virtue or +3 for the Major. Following the Sympathy rules of Realms of Power: The Faerie, she may add it in place of a specialty to a roll of a non-Supernatural Ability whenever she is acting directly on another woman, for instance to recall what she knows of a fellow maga. All rolls using this Trait must use stress dice. The Trait improves with experience as an Ability does, but cannot exceed her Warping Score +1 (Minor Virtue) or +3 (Major), and also rises by one when the stress roll comes up 1; it falls by one when a botch check comes up 0.

entries.name: Feminine Sympathy
entries.summary: Feminine Sympathy Trait +1 (Major: +3), added like a specialty to mundane Ability rolls that act directly on a woman; such rolls use stress dice.
entries.description: Initiated by the second level of the Matres and Matrones. The character gains a Sympathy Trait, Feminine Sympathy, at +1 for the Minor Virtue or +3 for the Major. Following the Sympathy rules of Realms of Power: The Faerie, she may add it in place of a specialty to a roll of a non-Supernatural Ability whenever she is acting directly on another woman, for instance to recall what she knows of a fellow maga. All rolls using this Trait must use stress dice. The Trait improves with experience as an Ability does, but cannot exceed her Warping Score +1 (Minor Virtue) or +3 (Major), and also rises by one when the stress roll comes up 1; it falls by one when a botch check comes up 0.

entries.name: Ferocity
entries.summary: 3 Confidence Points and Confidence Score 1, usable only when the animal's natural ferocity is triggered (e.g. defending its den).
entries.description: Like companion and magus characters, this character has Confidence points. However, these Confidence points may only be used in situations where its natural animal ferocity is triggered, such as when defending its den or fighting a natural enemy. Describe a situation which activates the Confidence for its species, and take 3 Confidence points and a Confidence Score of 1 to use when those circumstances are met.

entries.name: Fida'i
entries.summary: Nizari Isma'ili assassin trained in blades and disguise; Martial Abilities at creation; may rise to lasiq.
entries.description: The character is an assassin of the Nizari Isma'ilis. A fida'i is a devout member of the sect who is prepared to die on its orders, and as such he should consider taking either the Oath of Fealty or Dutybound Flaw. When not on a mission, a fida'i wears white, with a red girdle, cap, or boots. He has been trained in precise placement of daggers and blades, as well as disguise. Fida'i may take Martial Abilities at character creation. He can expect to become a lasiq if he proves his loyalty to the sect. This Social Status Virtue may be taken by a character who is living far from the home of the Nizaris, as the assassins are sent on missions, and may be sent far away. Such a character should have a Story Flaw representing his mission, and choose the Social Status he is pretending to have. See The Cradle and the Crescent, from page 162, for more detail on the Nizaris.

entries.name: Figurine Magic
entries.summary: Gain Ability Figurine Magic 1: make wax/wood figurines for one person imbued with a Minor Virtue or spell, lasting 6 or 12 months.
entries.description: Figurine Magic is an ancient tradition, the practice of installing magical affects into a carved figurine meant for a single recipient. Through these figurines wizards create lasting magical affects for others, typically mundane folk, those who could most benefit from these minor artifacts. Several forms of this type of magic exist, from antiquity through the Middle Ages, and Figurine Magic is one such form. This is an example of a non-hermetic practice of magic being integrated into Hermetic magic through a Major Breakthrough, making a teachable Supernatural Virtue. Figurines are small figures, constructed from wax or wood, that may be enchanted with Hermetic spells and effects that mirror Minor Virtues. Since the magus must make the figure himself, they are usually made from wax. The recipient of the figure must be determined before construction begins, since astrological charts particular to the subject must be drawn. Every magus knows how to generate astrological charts because astrology is one of the seven liberal arts covered by the Artes Liberales Ability. Since each figurine is made for a specific individual, the magus can not have a ready supply of figurines that can be easily doled out as the need arises. Constructing a figurine takes a month for a wax figurine or two for a wood figurine. The simplest figures are wax, and three can be made in a season if the crafter wishes. The difference in materials is the length of enchantment. Wax figures hold their magic for six months (two seasons), and wood figures for a year (four seasons). Regardless of the length of enchantment, if a figure is ever damaged or destroyed its magic ceases immediately. The better the figurine the stronger the magical attachment, so extreme care is taken constructing a figure. As the process begins, the magus must succeed with a Dexterity + Craft: Sculptor + stress roll against an Ease Factor of 6 for a wax figurine or 9 for a wood figurine. Failing this roll means the figurine is too crude to represent the target and the time spent constructing the figure is wasted. Botching this roll means the magus inadvertently constructed this figurine for someone else. He will not realize her mistake until the item fails to affect the target at the completion of the construction. Making a FIgure: Dexterity + Craft: Sculptor + Stress DieEase Factor: 6 for a Wax FIgurine, 9 for a Wood FIgure Remember that if a character does not have a score in Craft: Sculptor she may still make a roll, treating it as if she had a score of zero in the Ability and rolling three extra botch dice if necessary. Once the figure is carved it may be imbued with magic. Hermetic magi may enchant the figurines with Hermetic spells. They may also enchant the figurine with Minor General or Supernatural Virtues. The original practice only allows the enchantment of Minor Virtues. Integrating Figurine Magic into Hermetic magic allows the enchantment of Hermetic spells as well as the Virtues. The magus decides what sort of power the figurine will have at the beginning of the process. At the end of the figure's construction time, the magus rolls an Intelligence + Figurine Magic + Aura Modifier + stress die roll against an Ease Factor based on the magic imbued. Enchanting a FIgure: Intelligence + Figurine Magic + Aura Modifier Imbued Power and Ease Factor: Base 9 Minor General Virtue +3 Minor Supernatural Virtue +6 Hermetic Spell +1/magnitude Figurines imbued with a Supernatural Ability that requires a score, like Premonitions or Second Sight, allow the Figurine bearer to act as if she had a 1 in the specific Ability, which is then modified by any certain Characteristics according to the Virtue's description. Some General Virtues from the core ArM5 rules are inappropriate; they include Educated, Faerie Blood, Gossip, Improved Characteristic, Large, Latent Magic Ability, Privileged Upbringing, Protection, Relic, Skinchanger, Social Contacts, Student of (Realm), Troupe Upbringing, True Love (PC), Warrior, and Well-Traveled. Hermetic spells installed within an Figurine must have a range of Touch and a Target of Individual. The Duration of Sun is required, which is extended to constant use in the enchantment process, much like in the regular Laboratory rules section. The magus must be able to cast the desired spell he wishes to install within the figurine. Unlike a normal lesser enchanted item, the enchantment is not permanent. The figurine will hold the enchantment for a length of time dependent upon the material of the item, and the magic will eventually cease operating. Magi who can perform Figurine Magic prefer it to lesser enchanted items for three reasons. First, these creations do not require Vis to construct, merely time and effort. A magus' magical resources are not depleted when creating figurines. Secondly, they are quick to construct, requiring only a month instead of the usual season of laboratory time. Lastly, though they can be potent, they are an ephemeral magic, short-lived and fleeting. They are too weak to pester a magus, whose Parma Magica protects him from the figurine's magic. Enchanted figurines have a penetration total of zero. It would be interesting to move Figurine Magic out of the Supernatural Ability category and firmly incorporate it into Hermetic practices, allowing magi to simply make figurines without needing a corresponding Ability.
